rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: The address is said to have occurred in pre-eternity; another view identifies the messengers intended here as Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ولا محالة أن هذه المخاطبة في الأزل وقيل المراد بالرسل محمد عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Since Muhammad is the final prophet, the address is directed only to the children of Adam, because no others received it.
rows.anchor: المخاطبين هم المراد ببني آدم لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb يقصون means to recount or narrate.
rows.anchor: ويقُصون معناه يسردون ويوردون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آيات is a comprehensive term for revealed scriptures' verses and the signs accompanying prophets.
rows.anchor: لفظ جامع لآيات الكتب المنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من اتقى can be conditional, with فلا خوف عليهم as its answer.
rows.anchor: شرطية وجوابه فلا خوف عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, من اتقى is a relative clause that begins a division between the God-fearing and those who deny the signs.
rows.anchor: وكأنه قصد بالكلام تقسيم الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either parsing, the two groups answer the condition that messengers come; the message's consequence is safety for the pious and Hell for deniers.
rows.anchor: وجاء هذا التقسيم بجملته جوابا للشرط في قوله إما يأتينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about the greatest wrongdoer denies any worldly gain or purpose for fabricating against God; it exonerates the Prophet and rebukes disbelieving fabricators.
rows.anchor: ليس ثم نفع للمفتري ولا غرض دنياوي

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads لا خوف without tanwin; the tanwin may be dropped through frequent use or by analogy with its deletion after لا.
rows.anchor: دون تنوين، ووجهه إما أن يحذف التنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction of لا خوف is accusative, though its built form resembles the nominative; an alternative analysis treats it as فلا الخوف with the article deleted and retained ف marking it.
rows.anchor: وهي تبرية ناصبة تشبه حالة الرفع في البناء بحالة النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear and grief encompass every inner distress; fear likely concerns what is ahead and grief what has passed.
rows.anchor: ويشبه أن يكون الخوف لما يستقبل من الأمور والحزن لما مضى منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denial and arrogance are two general ways people resist a messenger: settled disbelief or arrogance that results in denial without settled conviction.
rows.anchor: إما أن يكذب بحسب اعتقاده وإما أن يستكبر فكذب وإن كان غير مصمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is like disbelief born of obstinacy.
rows.anchor: وهذا نحو الكفر عنادا

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: These readers pronounce ليَميز with an open yāʾ and kasra on mīm, from ماز; a rare reading انمازوا and Abu Zayd's line illustrate the verb's form and its passive-like separation.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة الأعرج وأبي جعفر وشيبة

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read ليميز with a prefixed ḍamma, open mīm, and doubled yāʾ, from ميّز meaning to separate; 67:8 uses تميز for things separating.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة قتادة وطلحة بن مصرف والأعمش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: They identify the vile as disbelievers and the good as believers.
rows.anchor: المعني ب الخبيث الكفار وب الطيب المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that interpretation, the purpose clause attaches to the disbelievers being gathered: God distinguishes them by gathering them together and casting them into Hell; losers are those whose effort failed and who ended there.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن الله يحشر الكافرين إلى جهنم

rows.speaker: ابن سلام والزجاج
rows.claim: They identify the vile as the wealth polytheists spent obstructing God's path and the good as believers' spending in God's path.
rows.anchor: المعني ب الخبيث المال الذي أنفقه المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this view, the purpose clause attaches to their being overcome: despite their spending, the disbelievers are defeated, so God distinguishes the groups by abandoning the vile and supporting the good.
rows.anchor: الكفار ينفقون أموالهم فتكون عليهم حسرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says God will bring out on Resurrection Day the wealth that was charity or an act of devotion, then order the rest thrown into the Fire.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أن الله تعالى يخرج من الأموال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the disbelievers are punished through that wealth; al-Zajjaj compares this to the Qur'anic threat that wealth will brand its owners.
rows.anchor: وحكى الزهراوي عن الحسن أن الكفار يعذبون بذلك المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On both interpretations, piling the vile together means collecting, joining, and compacting its scattered parts; ركم means to make dense, as in سحاب مركوم and Dhu al-Rumma's verse.
rows.anchor: إنما هي عبارة عن جمع ذلك وضمه وتأليف أشتاته

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains يجعل الخبيث as يلقي, 'casts'.
rows.anchor: بمعنى يلقي، قاله أبو علي، أولئك هم الخاسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the wealth interpretation, the losers are hypocrites among the disbelievers; the word loss suits them both financially and in other respects.
rows.anchor: على هذا التأويل يراد المنافقون من الكفار، ولفظة الخسارة تليق بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Prophet to convey the promise that ending disbelief brings forgiveness for the past; the message need not use these exact words.
rows.anchor: أمر من الله عز وجل لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقول للكفار هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i says Ibn Masud's codex reads يغفر لكم; Ibn Atiyya argues that if this were the wording, conveying the message would require those exact words.
rows.anchor: ذكر الكسائي أنه في مصحف ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they desist means desist from disbelief, since forgiveness of what preceded follows only when disbelief is abandoned.
rows.anchor: يريد به عن الكفر ولا بد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they return means return to fighting: absolute عاد يعود denotes resuming a former state one left, and fighting is the only such state in this passage; returning to disbelief is impossible because they remain in it.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح أن يتأول وإن يعودوا إلى الكفر لأنهم لم ينفصلوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic عاد can instead take a predicate and mean صار, 'became'; in that use it does not mean returning to a former state and cannot stand without its predicate, as Abu al-Salt's verse illustrates.
rows.anchor: لأنها قد تجيء في كلام العرب داخلة على الابتداء والخبر بمنزلة صار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past custom of earlier peoples is a threat recalling nations destroyed when they opposed their prophets and those killed at Badr by Islam's sword; the audience has seen or heard what happened.
rows.anchor: عبارة بجمع الوعيد والتهديد والتمثيل بمن هلك من الأمم في سالف الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's repentance means moving a servant from one state to a higher one, often from obedience to fuller obedience; for the Prophet it moves him from before the expedition and its merit to after it.
rows.anchor: من الله رجوعه بعبده من حالة إلى أرفع منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the Emigrants and Helpers, repentance may mean moving from shortcoming into obedience through the campaign and support of the religion.
rows.anchor: فحالها معرضة لأن تكون من تقصير إلى طاعة وجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the group whose hearts nearly swerved, it is a move from a lower state to forgiveness and approval.
rows.anchor: وأما توبته على الفريق الذي كاد أن يزيغ فرجوع من حالة محطوطة إلى حال غفران ورضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the Prophet means entering into his undertaking and setting out, without preferring oneself over him.
rows.anchor: دخلوا في أمره وانبعاثه ولم يرغبوا بأنفسهم عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here الساعة can mean a duration or period, though its ordinary Arabic sense is a short span of time; a Friday-prayer report uses first and second 'hours'.
rows.anchor: يريد في وقت العسرة فأنزل الساعة منزلة المدة والوقت والزمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the 'hour of hardship' may be the moment they resolved to bear the difficulty, when intention and reward attached; later prosperity would not change that description.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يريد بقوله في ساعة العسرة الساعة التي وقع فيها عزمهم وانقيادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عسرة means hardship, straitened circumstances, or lack, as in the verse about a debtor in hardship; this was the Army of Hardship.
rows.anchor: والعسرة الشدة وضيق الحال والعدم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that whoever equips the Army of Hardship earns Paradise; Uthman equipped it with a thousand camels and a thousand dinars.
rows.anchor: هذا هو جيش العسرة الذي قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيه: من جهز

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet turned Uthman's dinars in his hand and said that Uthman would not be harmed by what he did after this; an Ansari also brought seven hundred wasqs of dates.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قلب الدنانير بيده

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: They report that hardship at Tabuk became so severe that two men shared a date and groups successively chewed one date and drank water.
rows.anchor: مجاهد وقتادة: إن العسرة بلغت بهم

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar recounts extreme thirst: they slaughtered camels for stomach water and squeezed the dung; the Prophet prayed until rain fell, while a hypocrite dismissed the cloud as passing. Heat, crowds, and too few mounts compounded the hardship; the expedition reached the enemy's outskirts and made tribute agreements with Aḏruḥ, Aylah, and others.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: وأصابهم في بعضها عطش

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says one group nearly turned back because of the difficulty and hardship.
rows.anchor: همت فرقة بالانصراف لما لقوا من المشقة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another explanation is that their hearts nearly swerved through misgivings about the decision to campaign, given the hardship, poor supplies, long journey, and powerful enemy.
rows.anchor: وقيل زيغها إنما كان بظنون لها ساءت في معنى عزم رسول الله

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read تزيغ with tāʾ, matching the feminine plural قلوب; Abu Amr is also reported to assimilate dāl into tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس وأبو بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: حمزة وحفص عن عاصم والأعمش والجحدري
rows.claim: They read يزيغ with yāʾ, construing the hearts as a collective; Ibn Masud and Ubay have further variant readings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وحفص عن عاصم والأعمش

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh's strongest grammatical analysis makes كان refer to the story or situation, with القلوب as subject of تزيغ.
rows.anchor: القصة والشأن هذا مذهب سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing makes the implied subject of كان the people previously identified as Emigrants and Helpers: some of them nearly had hearts that swerved.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن يرتفع بها ما يقتضيه ذكر المهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing makes القلوب the subject of كان and treats تزيغ as containing a pronoun referring back to the hearts, by analogy with 30:47.
rows.anchor: وجاز ذلك تشبيها بكان في قوله كان حقا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali rejects extending this parsing to عسى; the fronted predicate is intended to be delayed, and كاد resembles كان because it requires its predicate.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي ولا يجوز ذلك في عسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then says He also repented toward this group and reassured the community by describing Himself as compassionate and merciful; the three are Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya al-Waqifi, and Murara ibn al-Rabi al-Amiri, also named Ibn Rabi'a or Ibn Rub'i.
rows.anchor: والثلاثة هم كعب بن مالك وهلال بن أمية الواقفي ومرارة بن الربيع العامري

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says خُلِّفوا means they were left behind from the Tabuk expedition; Ka'b himself rejects this, explaining that they were left pending acceptance of their excuses, not because they failed to join the campaign.
rows.anchor: هذا ضعيف وقد رده كعب بن مالك بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers 'left pending their excuse' because the constriction of the earth marks the endpoint of that decision, not the fact they had stayed behind from the campaign.
rows.anchor: ويقوي ذلك من اللفظة جعله إذا ضاقت غاية للتخليف

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read خُلِّفوا with ḍamma on خ and a doubled lām; other readers offer several vocalized forms, including المخلفين and خالفوا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «خلفوا» بضم الخاء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far says that if the word meant simply 'left behind' in the passive sense, the three would have had no sin.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر ولو خلفوا لم يكن لهم ذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بما رحبت means 'with its spaciousness,' with ما as a verbal noun; their selves narrowing is a metaphor for grief and distress filling them, and ظنوا means they knew with certainty.
rows.anchor: برحبها كأنه قال: على ما هي في نفسها رحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the passage counts blessings, it first names God's action in turning toward them so that they could repent; when recounting wrongdoing, the order instead begins with the wrongdoer, as in 61:5, to stress culpability.
rows.anchor: لما كان هذا القول في تعديد نعمه بدا في ترتيبه بالجهة التي هي عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode's full explanation depends on the detailed hadith of the three in the cited books; their sin was grave because the law expects greater diligence from people of standing, who serve as examples and evidence against hypocrites and critics. Ka'b was from al-Aqaba and his companions from Badr.
rows.anchor: وإنما عظم ذنبهم واستحقوا عليه ذلك لأن الشرع يطلبهم من الجد فيه بحسب منازلهم

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: In a letter to al-Mansur Abu Ja'far, al-Awza'i says kinship to the Prophet increases one's duty to God and obedience, and makes people's censure stronger when one acts against it; al-Tanukhi's verse likewise says a great person's fault is great.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن قرابتك من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لن تزيد حق الله عليك إلا عظما

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: One route says the Prophet was at Umm Salama's home on the night their repentance was revealed; when she offered to summon them, he said the crowds would keep them awake all night.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ليلة نزول توبتهم في بيت أم سلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to be with the truthful fits after the three's story: truth benefited them and removed them from the hypocrites' status, so the verse interrupts the narrative to mark its lesson.
rows.anchor: هذا الأمر بالكون مع أهل الصدق حسن بعد قصة الثلاثة حين نفعهم الصدق

rows.speaker: ابن جريج وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and others take truth in this verse to mean truthful speech.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج وغيره: الصدق في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: نافع والضحاك
rows.claim: Nafi and al-Dahhak understand truth more broadly as soundness in religion and steadfastness in goodness, like Arabic expressions for a 'true' tree or person; this group says believers should accompany Muhammad, Abu Bakr, Umar, and the truthful early Emigrants.
rows.anchor: وقال نافع والضحاك ما معناه:

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: They read وكونوا من الصادقين; a reading is also reported from the Prophet, and Ibn Masud interpreted it as truthfulness in speech.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says lying is wrong both seriously and jokingly, and cites this verse as evidence.
rows.anchor: الكذب لا يصلح منه جد ولا هزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adorned, boasting worldly life of wealth and children, which ends in extinction, is likened to rain that produces mixed growth.
rows.anchor: إذ يصير ذلك إلى الفناء

rows.speaker: فرقة من القراء
rows.claim: Some readers stop at فاختلط, taking it to mean that water mixed with earth, then resume with نبات الأرض as a new clause with a fronted predicate; به can refer to water or to the implied mixing.
rows.anchor: ثم استأنف به نبات الأرض على الابتداء

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group connects نبات as the subject of اختلط: plants mixed with one another because of the water.
rows.anchor: ووصلت فرقة فرفع «النبات» على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people eat means crops, trees, and similar growth; what livestock eat means all grazing herbage.
rows.anchor: يريد الزروع والأشجار ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخذت الأرض is a common idiom, as in 7:31; زخرف means colorful adornment and can also mean gold, from which it is made.
rows.anchor: التزين بالألوان، وقد يجيء الزخرف بمعنى الذهب

rows.speaker: مروان بن الحكم وأبو جعفر والسبعة وشيبة ومجاهد والجمهور
rows.claim: They read وازينت, from تزينت with tāʾ assimilated and a connecting alif; Ibn Masud, al-A'mash, and Ubay read the unassimilated وتزينت.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مروان بن الحكم وأبو جعفر والسبعة

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو العالية والشعبي وقتادة ونصر بن عاصم وعيسى
rows.claim: They read وأزينت as though the land had put on its adornment, analogous to أحصد الزرع; other recitations include وا زيانت, وازيأنت, and وازاينت, all meaning that its adornment appeared, with a poet's line cited for one form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو العالية والشعبي وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وظن أهلها is read in its ordinary sense; عليها refers to the earth and its blessings and plants. The whole worldly-life scene is compared to the described field.
rows.anchor: والضمير في عليها عائد على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى marks the endpoint and begins a clause with إذا; the description extends through the people's belief that they control the land, after which the outcome begins.
rows.anchor: وحتى غاية وهي حرف ابتداء لدخولها على إذا ومعناها متصل إلى قوله قادرون عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arriving أمر is a destructive force such as wind, cold, or simoom; specifying night or day warns that danger and loss of security can come at any time.
rows.anchor: والأمر الآتي واحد الأمور كالريح والصر والسموم ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حصيد is an active-form word with passive meaning, describing ruined vegetation whether harvested or destroyed by blight, as though calamity cut it down early.
rows.anchor: عن التالف الهالك من النبات وإن لم يهلك بحصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تغن means to flourish or thrive; Qatada reads يغن with yāʾ referring to the ruined crop, and Marwan reads كأن لم تتغن. المغاني means inhabited dwellings, supported by a poetic example.
rows.anchor: قرأ قتادة «يغن» بالياء من تحت يعني الحصيد

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubay's codex adds that the land would not have been destroyed except for its people's sins; this is transmitted by Ibn Abbas, with another version naming God as the subject.
rows.anchor: مصحف أبي بن كعب «كأن لم تغن بالأمس وما كنا لنهلكها

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reads لقوم يتذكرون in place of يتفكرون.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو الدرداء «لقوم يتذكرون»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable warns against being deluded by worldly life, which is exposed to destruction through death or other calamities; mentioning reflective people honors their rank and invites others to compete for it.
rows.anchor: إذ هي معرضة للتلف وأن يصيبها

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group lightens لكن and puts الناس in the nominative; another doubles لكن and puts الناس in the accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأت فرقة: «ولكن الناس» بتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People wrong themselves by their own acquisition, which accompanies God's creation of their acts.
rows.anchor: وظلم الناس لأنفسهم إنما هو بالتكسب منهم الذي يقارن اختراع الله تعالى لأفعالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لكن is normally heavy when preceded by wāw and light without it, though this pattern has exceptions; Kufans allow a lām in its predicate like إنّ, while Basrans reject it.
rows.anchor: أن تثقل وإذا عريت من الواو أن تخفف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering is a threat of humiliation and mutual reproach; يوم may be governed by an omitted اذكر, by the verb implied in كأن لم يلبثوا, or by يتعارفون.
rows.anchor: وعيد بالحشر وخزيهم فيه وتعاونهم في التلاوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with a daytime hour can modify the day, serve as an absolute accusative, or be circumstantial; daytime is specified because its familiar divisions make the shortness of their stay vivid.
rows.anchor: وخصص النهار بالذكر لأن ساعاته وقسمه معروفة بينة للجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يتعارفون may describe mutual recognition and reproach at Resurrection, or be circumstantial from the gathering; alternatively it describes recognition in worldly life, whose ties will seem no longer than an hour at Resurrection, as al-Tabari explains.
rows.anchor: وهذا التعارف على جهة التلاوم والخزي من بعضهم

rows.speaker: السبعة وجمهور الناس
rows.claim: They read نحشرهم with nūn; a report from al-A'mash has يحشرهم with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السبعة وجمهور الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verdict calls deniers losers and exposes their delusion about God; the words may be God's report or the gathered people's self-reproach.
rows.anchor: حكم على المكذبين بالخسار وفي اللفظ إغلاظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إما نرينك is a conditional construction answered by فإلينا; نرينك is a form-IV visual seeing with two objects, 'you' and 'some of what We promise,' such as punishment at Badr.
rows.anchor: والرؤية في قوله نرينك رؤية بصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether the Prophet sees some punishment or not, the disbelievers return for judgment and punishment; God has witnessed all their deeds since their moral obligation began, and ثم orders the account's presentation rather than events in time.
rows.anchor: ومعنى هذه الآية الوعيد بالرجوع إلى الله تعالى أي إن أريناك عقوبتهم أو لم نركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إما consists of إن plus ما, which permits the emphatic nūn; إن alone would not permit it.
rows.anchor: ولأجلها جاز دخول النون الثقيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every nation has a messenger, as in the scene where the keepers of Hell ask each arriving group whether a warner came.
rows.anchor: كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: Mujahid and others say each nation's messenger comes on Resurrection Day to testify; people are then assigned to Paradise or Fire, which is judgment in equity.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره: المعنى فإذا جاء رسولهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another view places the messenger's coming in worldly life: God's decree then assigns punishment or forgiveness according to people's ends; the relation to 17:15 works if punishment is in the afterlife or judgment occurs in this world.
rows.anchor: المعنى فإذا جاء رسولهم في الدنيا وبعث صاروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers ask for the promised punishment's date as a challenge to establish truth or falsehood; some say they ask mockingly, but Ibn Atiyya says that tone is not apparent from the wording.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يظهر من اللفظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to say he controls neither harm nor benefit for himself apart from God's will and remains under God's power and need of His grace; therefore he cannot claim knowledge of the unseen or defy God's command.
rows.anchor: إني لا أملك لنفسي ضرا ولا نفعا من دون الله ولا أنا إلا في قبضة سلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each nation's term is known only to God; when death or destruction comes, it cannot be delayed or brought forward by even an hour.
rows.anchor: ولكن لكل أمة أجل انفرد الله تعالى بعلم حده ووقته

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin reads آجالهم in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن سيرين «آجالهم» بالجمع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reads وجوزنا with a doubled wāw and no alif; Ibn Atiyya suggests جاوزنا may have been written without alif in some codices.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن «وجوزنا»

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read فأتبعهم, since تبع and أتبع can both mean 'follow'; Qatada and Hasan read فاتبعهم, which Abu Hatim distinguishes as pursuit of the trail whether or not the pursuer catches up.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «فأتبعهم» لأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports of six hundred thousand Israelites and eight hundred thousand of Pharaoh's dark horses, and smaller variants, are all weak; the Qur'an indicates many Israelites but fewer than Pharaoh's pursuing people.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله ضعيف، والذي تقتضيه ألفاظ القرآن

rows.speaker: الجمهور ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكوفيون
rows.claim: The readers differ over the vocalization of عدوًا: most read it on the pattern of غزا, while Hasan and Qatada use the form غزوا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكوفيون وجماعة عدوا على مثال غزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel entered the sea on a mare while Pharaoh followed on his stallion; Michael drove the troops into the sea, which then closed over them, and Pharaoh spoke the words quoted in the verse.
rows.anchor: فبعث الله جبريل على فرس أنثى وديق

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read أنه with fatḥa, either as an accusative or with an omitted preposition; Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Amr read إنه with kasra, either after an implied 'I said' or as a new clause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «أنه» بفتح الألف

rows.speaker: جبريل عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says Gabriel hated Pharaoh most, heard him profess faith, and put sea mud in his mouth lest mercy reach him; another version says Gabriel feared he would utter the testimony of God's oneness.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's speech shows confusion and faltering; ignorance of the known God is no excuse, unlike matters inaccessible to knowledge, as in Ali's statement about making the Prophet's talbiya.
rows.anchor: كلام فرعون ففيه مجهلة وتلعثم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: When the definite article precedes a word beginning with hamza that is softened, one may delete the hamza and move its vowel to lām, or delete the connecting hamza as well; Sibawayh and Abu al-Hasan attest these forms, with a poem cited as evidence.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن لام المعرفة إذا دخلت على كلمة أولها الهمزة فخففت الهمزة فإن في تخفيفها وجهين

rows.speaker: نافع عن ورش
rows.claim: Warsh from Nafi reads الآن with a prolonged hamza and open lām; other readers prolong the first hamza, leave lām unvocalized, and pronounce the second hamza, while additional readings shorten or soften the hamzas.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع في رواية ورش لم يختلف عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The softened-hamza readings follow Abu Ali's analysis; the wording reproaches Pharaoh and announces punishment, and may be an actual message delivered by an angel or a portrayal of his state and humiliation.
rows.anchor: وهذا اللفظ يحتمل أن يكون مسموعا لفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse explicitly shows that repentance after witnessing death is not accepted.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية نص في رد توبة المعاين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about saving Pharaoh's body supports reading the preceding speech as a portrayal of his state, since the body was cast ashore after death; the Israelites had thought him too mighty to die, and some denied his drowning until all saw him dead.
rows.anchor: على نجوة من الأرض حتى رآه جميعهم ميتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns and urges faith: persistence in disbelief brings punishment while faith brings rescue, following God's way with earlier nations; the question rebukes, and 'wait' offers a truce that fighting later superseded.
rows.anchor: حل بهم العذاب، وإذا آمنوا نجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the punishment's duration is unspecified while the Prophet and believers remain among disbelievers, God explicitly states that His established practice is to rescue messengers and their followers, making the threat more severe.
rows.anchor: لما كان العذاب لم تحصر مدته وكان النبي والمؤمنون بين أظهر الكفرة وقع التصريح

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: All but al-Kisa'i and Hafs read ننجي with a doubled jīm; they read it with a quiescent first nūn and a light jīm. Other reported forms are called baseless by al-Zajjaj, and the written form omits yāʾ after jīm.
rows.anchor: وكلهم قرأ «ننجي» مشددة الجيم إلا الكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كذلك can be nominative or accusative as an adjective describing an omitted verbal noun.
rows.anchor: يصح أن تكون في موضع رفع، ويصح أن تكون في موضع نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes all people through the end of time who doubt Islam; eloquent compression omits the implied statement that doubters do not worship God before naming the true object of worship.
rows.anchor: مخاطبة عامة للناس أجمعين إلى يوم القيامة يدخل تحتها كل من اتصف بالشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is singled out as the one who causes death to recall mortality, return to God, and the loss of idols believed to harm or benefit.
rows.anchor: وخص من أوصافه الذي يتوفاكم لما فيها من التذكير للموت وقرع النفوس به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation has Muhammad address the disbelievers: if those challenged cannot produce a counterpart, they should acknowledge its divine origin and submit; another has God address believers to remain certain of what they already know.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن تكون المخاطبة من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم للكفار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says 'Are you submitting?' is addressed to Muhammad's Companions.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: قوله تعالى: فهل أنتم مسلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بعلم الله may mean by God's permission and knowledge, or that the revelation contains what God knows of unseen matters; فهل أنتم مسلمون is an interrogative demanding acknowledgment.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: بعلم الله يحتمل معنيين

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: They take the universal wording about seeking worldly life as specifically referring to disbelievers.
rows.anchor: فرقة: ظاهرها العموم ومعناها الخصوص في الكفرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid includes disbelievers and believers who act for show; Muawiya adopted this after Shafi ibn Mati al-Asbahi relayed the Prophetic report about a charity-giver, slain fighter, and Qur'an-reciter whose ostentation makes them first fuel for Hell, then wept and cited the passage.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: هي في الكفرة وفي أهل الرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the disbeliever reading, يريد means to intend and aim: worldly life is the person's sole goal, without belief in an afterlife; God repays good deeds with worldly favors, though provision may be narrow or ample, and their afterlife is only Fire.
rows.anchor: فمعنى قوله يريد يقصد ويعتمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the disbeliever interpretation because the preceding context concerns those opposing the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: بحسب تقدم ذكر الكفار المناقضين في القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: On the view that the passage includes sinful believers, يريد means love, prefer, and choose; God rewards good deeds not done for Him with worldly favors, while 'only Fire' means it is what they deserve, though God may forgive them.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو ظاهر ألفاظ ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas says the verses concern the People of the Book; Ibn Atiyya says they are included as disbelievers, not the exclusive referent.
rows.anchor: أنس بن مالك: هي في أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read نوف with the majestic first-person nūn; Talha and Maymun ibn Mihran read يوف with a third-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «نوف» بنون العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يبخسون means they are given less than their reward.
rows.anchor: معناه: يعطون أقل من ثوابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حبط means to become void or fall away, used of corrupted deeds; the Prophet's phrase يقتل حبطا أو يلم illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: يبطل وسقط ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in فيها first refers to worldly life and in its third occurrence to the afterlife; alternatives make all three refer to this world or the second to deeds.
rows.anchor: عائد على الدنيا في الأولين وفي الثالثة عائد على الآخرة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read وباطل in the nominative; Ubay and Ibn Masud read وباطلا in the accusative, attested in four codices, with يعملون governing it and ما treated as extra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «وباطل» بالرفع على الابتداء والخبر، وقرأ أبي وابن مسعود: «وباطلا» بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: باطل is anything whose nature prevents it from attaining a final end such as reward.
rows.anchor: والباطل كل ما تقتضي ذاته أن لا تنال به غاية في ثواب ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's son thought the flood was ordinary rain and water.
rows.anchor: ظن ابن نوح أن ذلك المطر والماء على العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes عاصم literally as the active participle; إلا من رحم means 'except God, the Merciful,' with من standing for God and in the nominative.
rows.anchor: يريد إلا الله الراحم، ف من كناية عن اسم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another analysis treats the exception as disconnected: no protector exists, but one whom God has mercy on exists; this suits the meaning that denying a rescuer entails denying someone rescued, with من accusative, as in al-Nabigha's exception.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع كأنه قال: لا عاصم

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A further view takes عاصم as one possessing protection, effectively meaning protected; then the exception is regular and من is nominative. A raised exception cannot follow the line about a desolate place, since its gazelles and camels are truly companions whereas the saved son is no protector.
rows.anchor: وقيل عاصم معناه ذو اعتصام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اليوم modifies من أمر الله or an understood 'good' that exists today, not عاصم, which would wrongly leave the word without tanwin; the syntactic rule is illustrated by لا أمرا يوم الجمعة لك versus لا أمر.
rows.anchor: واليوم ظرف، وهو متعلق بقوله: من أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بينهما means between Noah and his son, and the son was among those drowned.
rows.anchor: وبينهما يريد بين نوح وابنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line about what diminished from sight and limbs illustrates the drying and wasting of old age.
rows.anchor: ما غيض من بصري ومن أجلادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya explains that old age reduces a person through drying and shrinking.
rows.anchor: الإنسان الهرم إنما تنقصه بجفوف وقضافة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Al-Tabari cites Ibn Ishaq as implying that Noah remained on the water for about a year.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق ما يقتضي أنه أقام على الماء نحو السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقضي الأمر refers to the whole story: the flood, the destruction of peoples, and the rescue of the ark occupants.
rows.anchor: وقوله وقضي الأمر إشارة إلى جميع القصة: بعث الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقضي الأمر refers to the whole story: the flood's onset, the peoples' destruction, and the ark's occupants being saved.
rows.anchor: وقوله وقضي الأمر إشارة إلى جميع القصة: بعث الماء

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Reports place the ark's departure from Ain Warda in Syria on the first, tenth, fifteenth, or seventeenth of Rajab; it settled on Judi in Dhu al-Hijja for a month, and Noah was told to disembark on Ashura and fast. Ibn Ishaq's account implies nearly a year on the water; a Prophetic report says Noah sailed on the first of Rajab, fasted the month, and landed on Judi at Ashura, which he and his companions fasted.
rows.anchor: وروي أن نوحا عليه السلام ركب في السفينة من عين وردة بالشام أول يوم من رجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Noah sent a raven for news; it stayed at a floating carcass, so he cursed it black and people feared it. A dove returned with an olive leaf but no dry place, then after forty days found mud as the water receded from the Kaaba, the first land exposed; Noah blessed it, and it became tame.
rows.anchor: وروي أن نوحا لما طال مقامه على الماء بعث الغراب ليأتيه بخبر كمال الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says the mountains competed for the ark, but humble Judi did not rise; the ark landed there in Mosul's Jazira region, leaving planks, and a Prophetic report says some remained until the early Muslim community. Al-Zajjaj places Judi near Amid, while others place it near Baqarda.
rows.anchor: واحد منها فتطاولت كلها وبقي الجودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the ark went from Ain Warda to the Kaaba, which had risen above the flood; it circled it seven times, went to Yemen, then returned to Judi.
rows.anchor: وروي أن السفينة لما استقلت من عين وردة جرت حتى جاءت الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many transmitted stories are difficult to cover fully and conflict, as in the Kaaba account; Ibn Atiyya offers only examples and leaves the exact truth to God. استوت means settled firmly.
rows.anchor: في هذه المعاني كثير صعب أن يستوفي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most read الجودي with kasra and a doubled yāʾ; al-A'mash and Ibn Abi Abla leave the yāʾ quiescent, two dialect forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «على الجودي» بكسر الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقيل بعدا may continue God's passive narration or be words of Noah and the believers; the first is stronger and more eloquent.
rows.anchor: بعدا يحتمل أن يكون من قول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Prophet is already upright, the command means to continue and remain steadfast, like telling someone already walking or eating to keep doing so; the address includes him and the Companions who repented from disbelief, and by implication the whole community.
rows.anchor: أمر النبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالاستقامة وهو عليها إنما هو أمر بالدوام والثبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scholar reportedly saw the Prophet in a dream and asked what in Hud made him say it and its companion suras had made him gray; the Prophet answered, 'Be steadfast as you were commanded.' Ibn Atiyya says the well-known explanation is his fear that earlier peoples' fates might befall this community.
rows.anchor: رأي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في النوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمرت is an honorific plural form of address; ومن is coordinated with the pronoun in فاستقم, permitted without repeating it because كما أمرت makes the phrase long.
rows.anchor: ومن معطوف على الضمير في قوله: فاستقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا تطغوا means do not exceed God's limits; طغيان is crossing the limit, as with the flood and Pharaoh, or specifically letting blessings lead to transgression.
rows.anchor: معناه: ولا تتجاوزوا حدود الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read تعملون with second-person tāʾ; Hasan and al-A'mash read يعملون with third-person yāʾ, and readers vary between open and rounded kaf in تركنوا, with the latter a dialect form meaning to settle or be content with something.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «تعملون» بتاء، وقرأ الحسن والأعمش «يعملون»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ركن إلى الشيء means to settle with and be content with it; Abu al-Aliyya cites a poem after this gloss.
rows.anchor: معناه السكون، إلى الشيء والرضا به قال أبو العالية:

rows.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
rows.claim: Most early interpreters take the good deeds that erase sins as the five prayers; Uthman invoked this verse while performing ablution, and this is Malik's interpretation.
rows.anchor: ذهب جمهور المتأولين من صحابة وتابعين إلى أن الحسنات يراد بها الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the good deeds are a person's repeated glorification, praise, profession of divine unity, and magnification of God.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الحسنات: قول الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are examples of good deeds; the verse's wording is general for good deeds but specific to lesser sins in light of the Prophetic phrase 'if major sins are avoided.'
rows.anchor: وهذا كله إنما هو على جهة المثال في الحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the verse came after an Ansari man—identified as Abu al-Yusr ibn Amr or as Abbad—met a woman alone and kissed and fondled her without intercourse; after he told Umar and Abu Bakr, he confessed to the Prophet, who recited the verse. Muadh asked if it was only for him; the Prophet said it was for everyone. Another report says the verse predated the incident and was applied to him.
rows.anchor: وروي أن هذه الآية نزلت في رجل من الأنصار

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said Friday to Friday, the five prayers, and Ramadan to Ramadan expiate what lies between them if major sins are avoided.
rows.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الجمعة إلى الجمعة

rows.speaker: جمهور أهل السنة
rows.claim: Most Sunni scholars make avoiding major sins a condition of the entire promise: without it, the named acts do not expiate lesser sins.
rows.anchor: فقال جمهورهم: هو شرط في معنى الوعد كله

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says major sins are the sins the acts do not erase; the condition preserves the hadith's broad wording while the acts still erase lesser sins.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: معنى قوله إن اجتنبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya adopts the second interpretation: the hadith about sins falling away with drops of water supports it, provided minor sins are repented of and not persisted in; he calls this the precise view of expert legal theorists. On the first interpretation, the verse applies only to those who avoid major sins.
rows.anchor: وبهذا أقول وهو الذي يقتضيه حديث خروج الخطايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك may refer to the prayers as a cause and setting for remembrance, to the claim that good deeds erase sins as encouragement toward good deeds, or to all the preceding commands and prohibitions, as al-Tabari explains.
rows.anchor: أي هي سبب ذكر وموضع ذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence says God repays everyone for good and bad deeds, commands steadfastness, promises reward for prayer, then patience in preaching and hardship, and promises not to waste the good-doers' reward.
rows.anchor: أعلمه الله تعالى أنه يوفي جميع الخلائق أعمالهم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari takes the woman's words to mean: 'This is the man over whom you blamed me,' the one whose sake made her err in passion; the pronoun in فيه refers to Joseph. Alternatively, the gesture is to her love of Joseph and the pronoun refers to that love.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: المعنى: فهذا الذي لمتنني فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife of al-Aziz admits to seducing Joseph and appeals to the women because she knows they excuse her; استعصم means he sought and held to protection, before she threatens him while he hears.
rows.anchor: ثم أقرت امرأة العزيز للنسوة بالمراودة واستنامت إليهن في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ليسجنن the first lām introduces an oath, the next is the oath lām, and the nūn is emphatic and doubled at pause; وليكونا has a light nūn and pauses with alif, like 96:15 and the line of al-A'sha. A group reads its nūn doubled; الصاغرين are the humiliated.
rows.anchor: لام القسم، واللام الأولى هي المؤذنة بمجيء القسم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When the wife threatened Joseph, the women urged him to obey their mistress and do what she ordered; Hasan gives a similar account, explaining his phrase 'what they invite me to.'
rows.anchor: قال له النسوة: أطع مولاتك، وافعل ما أمرتك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يدعون here has the pattern يفعلن, unlike the masculine plural يدعون.
rows.anchor: يفعلن، بخلاف قولك: الرجال يدعون

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read السجن with kasra as the noun 'prison'; al-Zuhri, Ibn Hurmuz, Yaqub, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with fatḥa as the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «السجن» بكسر السين، وهو الاسم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: The cited poems of Hind and Duraid ibn al-Simma illustrate صبا from الصبوة, youthful inclination or infatuation.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قول دريد بن الصمة: [الطويل] صبا ما صبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ignorant are those who do not observe God's limits and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: والجاهلين هم الذين لا يراعون حدود الله تعالى ونواهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's prayer from 'Lord, prison' through 'one of the ignorant' both complains to God about his situation with the women and asks Him to remove the affliction; God's response means granting his wish and preventing the sin by blocking their scheme.
rows.anchor: إلى الله عز وجل من حاله معهن، والدعاء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing and knowing are fitting attributes after God answers Joseph's prayer.
rows.anchor: صفتان لائقتان بقوله: فاستجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Joseph refused sin, the wife of al-Aziz allegedly told her husband that the Hebrew boy had publicly disgraced her and was explaining matters on his own terms; she demanded either release so she could defend herself and accuse him, or his imprisonment while she remained confined. They then chose prison.
rows.anchor: ويئست منه امرأة العزيز طالبته بأن قالت لزوجها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph was put on a donkey, a drum was beaten, and he was announced through Egypt's markets as a Hebrew who desired his master and deserved prison; Abu Salih says Ibn Abbas wept whenever recounting it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فأمر به فحمل على حمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بدا means appeared, with a deleted subject estimated as بدو or رأي; the plural لهم refers to the king alone because the decision involved consultation, and ليسجننه is an oath clause.
rows.anchor: ظهر، والفاعل ب بدا محذوف تقديره

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh's explicit position is that ليسجننه cannot be the grammatical subject of بدا, since a sentence cannot be its subject; the claim that it is the subject is wrong, and the sentence instead explains the omitted subject.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون الفاعل ببدا ليسجننه لأن الفاعل لا يكون جملة بوجه

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: Interpreters identify the signs as the torn shirt; Ikrima says Joseph's scratched face accompanied the shirt episode, and al-Suddi says the women cut their hands.
rows.anchor: أنها قد القميص، قاله مجاهد وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is that they decided on prison after signs had exonerated Joseph; scratched faces and cut hands do not prove innocence, whereas the shirt report does. If the speaker was an infant it was a great miracle; if an adult, the shirt offered an inference. 'Signs' may also mean whatever proofs were clear in degree.
rows.anchor: ومقصد الكلام إنما هو أنهم رأوا سجنه بعد بدو الآيات المبرئة له من التهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, 'after they saw the signs' may mean that the overall circumstances showed Joseph was innocent, without identifying any one specific sign.
rows.anchor: أي من بعد ما ظهر لهم من وجوه الأمر
